notes: Direct HTTP fetch of the live site is blocked by a DataDome bot-challenge (robots.txt itself is reachable and lists no Claude-specific Disallow: / block, so no policy_opt_out). Headless Playwright hit the same DataDome CAPTCHA. Used the Claude-in-Chrome connector (tier 3) to reach the real, rendered site; from there, page-context fetch() calls (same-origin, past the challenge) were used to read the site's own sitemap-category.xml/sitemap-virtual-category.xml/sitemap-openfacet.xml and each category page's HTML/DOM, which is HTTP-first reading of the site's own data, not a proxy/cache substitute. Discovery: checked main nav (PRODUITS mega-menu, IDEES DECO, PIECES) - no seasonal branch is exposed in top nav in early September; checked internal search for 'noel'/'decoration noel' (non-discriminating default-ish results, used only for discovery per rules) which surfaced a 'Categorie' facet naming real category nodes; confirmed and completed the taxonomy via the 3 sitemap files and by walking each category page's own breadcrumb + sibling-tab pills back to the root 'Toute la collection Noel'. This produced a complete, verified 7-branch Christmas tree (23 rows). Excluded 'Stickers Noel' (child of Decorations de Noel): page returns 'cette page n'est plus disponible' (discontinued/dead), dropped per 0/dead-category rule. 'Papiers cadeaux' and 'Pochettes cadeaux' have generic (non-'Noel') titles but their only breadcrumb path is Accueil > Toute la collection Noel > <name>, i.e. the site's own taxonomy files them exclusively as part of the Christmas collection, so they are kept (Rule 7 coexistence). Searched all 3 sitemaps (category/virtual-category/openfacet, ~16000 URLs combined) plus live site search for halloween/paques/valentin/epiphanie/chandeleur/fete-des-meres: zero genuine category matches for any holiday other than Christmas (the 3 'halloween' search hits are black-coloured Christmas trees, not a Halloween category). No Halloween/Easter/Valentine's/Mother's-Day/etc. categories exist on this site. Qty method: category pages showing 'Vous avez vu X produits sur Y' pagination text use Y (site's own exact total, cross-verified against the 'Y articles' summary line shown on-page); pages with no next-page control were fully enumerated by counting unique product-card DOM nodes after full render (verified stable across repeated navigations/fetches). Parent/child sums are not always additive (e.g. Decorations de Noel's children sum to more than its own total) because a product can sit in more than one sibling sub-category on this site; each row's qty is that row's own site-reported number, never inferred from siblings.
